column1: *** AND IT IS NOT ORGANISED THE WAY THE WORD "ALPHABETICAL" SUGGESTS ***
column2: WITHIN EACH LETTER THE ENTRIES RUN BY YEAR, not by second letter — a heading "1895.", then that year's deaths under that letter numbered from 1, then "1896.", and so on. SO YOU CANNOT SKIM FOR A SURNAME; you read the whole letter. That is the slot method arriving as a physical object.

column1: and it runs past its own title
column2: the cover says 1894 to 1908; THE ENTRIES CONTINUE TO 1911, in a later hand and in POLISH — "żona robotnika", "córka krawca", "wdowa" — where the earlier pages are German. The volume outlived the state that opened it.

column1: # ---------------- *** THE NEGATIVE THIS OVERTURNS — THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN *** ----------------
*** szubin-death-registers-searched.tsv SAID THERE IS NO ALPHABETICAL DEATH INDEX, AND SAID IT WITH A CONTROL ***
column2: That row reads: "The portal carries SKOROWIDZE for Szubin, and they exist for BIRTHS and for MARRIAGES. Filtering to SKOROWIDZE ZGONÓW returns ZERO. THE CONTROL IS THAT THE SAME FACET WORKS... So the zero is a real absence and not a broken filter. DEATHS AT SZUBIN HAVE NO NAME INDEX AND MUST BE PAGED." THE REASONING WAS SOUND AND THE CONCLUSION WAS WRONG.

column1: what was actually true
column2: THE INDEX EXISTS AND IS SIMPLY NOT PUBLISHED ON THE PORTAL. The zero was a fact about genealogiawarchiwach.pl and this archive turned it into a fact about the holdings of the Archiwum Państwowe w Bydgoszczy. A CATALOGUE IS NOT AN ARCHIVE. The portal shows what has been digitised and put online; the archive holds what it holds, and the only instrument that can tell you the difference is a letter to the archivist.

column1: and the cost of the error was the size of the row it blocked
column2: row 264 costed Sally Leibholz's death at "190 death units, no index, no year — an open-ended read, not a check" AND RECOMMENDED BERLIN FIRST ON THAT BASIS. With this volume the Szubin question is FOUR PAGES.

column1: *** THERE IS NO LEIBHOLZ IN IT ***
column2: and the absence is bracketed at both ends by a name and by a year, which is what this archive means by a negative.

column1: *** AND THE SLOT CARRIES ITS OWN CONTROL, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE NEGATIVE ***
column2: THE INSTRUMENT WAS NOT BLIND TO JEWS. The very first entry in the L slot is LEHMANN MOSES, Schneider, 1894, and the 1909 entries open with LEISER ADOLF. Elsewhere in the volume: SAMUEL, SILBERBERG, SALZBRUNN, SCHOBELT. A Jewish death at Schubin after 1874 went into the civil register like anybody else's, AND THIS INDEX LISTS THEM. So the missing Leibholz is missing because he is not there, not because the book would have left him out.

column1: what that does and does not mean
column2: JUDA SCHMUL AND JETTE MACHOT DID NOT DIE AT SZUBIN TOWN BETWEEN 1894 AND 1911, nor did FRIEDERICA. It does not touch 1874-1893, when parents born in the 1820s are at least as likely to have died, and it does not touch the two Szubin WIEŚ registry offices.

column1: # ---------------- THE BOUNDS, STATED BEFORE ANYBODY ASKS ----------------
what is NOT covered, and it is the more likely window for Sally
column2: THE VOLUME BEGINS IN 1894. Sally Leibholz was alive at Schubin in August 1884, when he registered his son Jacob's birth in person, and he was born in 1847. A DEATH BETWEEN 1884 AND 1893 IS ENTIRELY UNCOVERED BY THIS BOOK and is arguably the likelier window for a man who would have been only 46 in 1894. The archive should now ask Bydgoszcz whether an equivalent index exists for 1874-1893.

column1: and it is one office of three
column2: this is STANDESAMT SCHUBIN — the town, 6/1792. Szubin also had USC SZUBIN WIEŚ I (6/1795) and WIEŚ II (6/1796), and this volume says nothing about either.

column1: so row 264 is narrowed, not closed
column2: Sally Leibholz still has no death date. What has changed is that the largest single candidate window at his own town is now read out, cheaply, from an index that was said not to exist.
